overall: A curious, warm explainer from someone who has stood in the yard and finds the box-at-the-bottom gag a little funny. The read stays conversational and level, dips to its quietest on the vendor's twenty percent ceiling so the caveat is heard, and lands low and certain on the last line.

lines.text: A truck rolls into Port Houston for one orange container. It sits at the bottom of a stack, buried under other boxes.
lines.intent: Open on the gag and set the picture
lines.note: Plain and easy, like starting a story. Weight on 'orange'. A small dry smile on 'bottom of a stack', then 'buried under other boxes' lands flat.

lines.text: So the crane has to dig, lifting box after box to reach it, while the driver waits below.
lines.intent: Show the cost of the problem
lines.note: Slight wry lift on 'dig'. 'Three extra lifts' is the weight of the line. 'While the driver waits below' trails off a little, patient.

lines.text: Port Houston was managing 142 of these rubber-tired gantry cranes at its Barbours Cut and Bayport terminals, on the Houston Ship Channel.
lines.intent: Establish scale and place with facts
lines.note: Informational and unhurried. Say it like a local reading off the sign. Barbours Cut is BAR-berz, Bayport is BY-port. Weight on 142, nothing pushed after it.

lines.text: Those terminals see up to 12,000 truck visits a day, and a driver picking up comes for one particular box.
lines.intent: Raise the stakes for the one driver
lines.note: Number said plainly. The turn to 'one particular box' narrows and gets a touch more personal.

lines.text: The pressure keeps building. 2025 was a record year for containers at Port Houston, and volumes are forecast to keep growing.
lines.note: The short first sentence carries the lift. Read 'twenty twenty-five' as a year. Keep 'forecast' honest and neutral. No drum roll.

lines.text: So which move should a crane make next? Software from a company called Kaleris now helps decide.
lines.note: A real question, curious rather than rhetorical. Drop the pitch after it, then 'Kaleris' is stated casually as a name. Kaleris is kuh-LAIR-iss.

lines.text: It is called RTG Optimization. It plans the order of crane moves to avoid blocked stacks, inside the terminal's own operating system.
lines.intent: Name the tool and say what it does
lines.note: Spell out R, T, G clearly. Weight on 'order'. 'Inside the terminal's own operating system' is a quiet aside, matter of fact.

lines.text: It sends cranes where the demand is, using better data on what the yard needs.
lines.intent: Explain the mechanism in plain words
lines.note: Simple and slightly slower, explaining to a friend. Weight on 'demand'. No sales gloss on 'better data'.

lines.text: It didn't start everywhere at once. The rollout began with truck moves in one small section of the yard.
lines.note: Reassuring and grounded. 'Everywhere at once' gets a gentle shake of the head, then 'one small section' is said smaller.

lines.text: Lessons from those early stages became custom filters and workflow changes that improved the operators' experience.
lines.intent: Show learning feeding back into the tool
lines.note: Even and practical. Weight on 'operators'' so the people stay in the sentence.

lines.text: People still run the cranes. Port Houston operations chief Ryan Mariacher says the system works in tandem with the skilled labor of the ILA, the International Longshoremen's Association.
lines.intent: Land the human point and attribute it
lines.note: 'People still run the cranes' is short, firm and warm. The attribution is then read as a clean report. Mariacher is MAR-ee-AH-kur. Say ILA as three letters, then the full name steady and respectful.

lines.text: Kaleris reports up to a 20 percent gain in yard crane productivity. That is the company's own figure, and up to means a ceiling.
lines.intent: Deliver the number with its honest caveat
lines.note: Quietest line of the film. The figure goes in flat with no lift on 'percent'. 'The company's own figure' is dry and fair. 'A ceiling' is said last, quiet and certain.

lines.text: So back to that truck. This time the orange box is already on top. Same crane, same hands, a better next move.
lines.intent: Close the loop and pay off the gag
lines.note: A small warm smile on 'already on top', the gag resolved. The last sentence settles lower than the middle of the film, three even beats, finished and unhurried, no rise on 'move'.
